sections.html:
Daphne is a city in Baldwin County on the eastern shore of Mobile Bay, along Interstate 10 about 11 miles east of Mobile. It is the most populous city in Baldwin County and a principal city of the Daphne, Fairhope and Foley metropolitan area, which covers all of the county.

Locals call Daphne, Spanish Fort to the north and Fairhope to the south the Eastern Shore. The land slopes gently from sea level on the west to low rolling hills further east, and the city lies no more than about 150 feet above sea level. The nickname Jubilee City comes from the Mobile Bay jubilee, when crabs, shrimp and other sea life wash ashore.

sections.h2: What is the history of Daphne?
sections.html:
The community was established in 1763 and was known simply as the Village, serving as the eastern end of a ferry across Mobile Bay. The area became part of the United States in 1814, after Andrew Jackson crossed the bay with 3,000 troops.

Daphne was named the Baldwin County seat in 1868, and kept that role until a 1900 legislative act moved it to Bay Minette. Italian immigrants arrived in 1888, and the Catholic church they built in what is now Old Daphne was served by its first resident pastor from 1898 to 1909. The town was incorporated on July 8, 1927, with 41 landowners signing the request.

A toll bridge to Mobile opened in 1929, the same year US 98 was paved through Daphne. Until then the town had been quite isolated from the larger city across the water.

sections.h2: How big is Daphne, and how fast is it growing?
sections.html:
Daphne has grown from 3,406 people in 1980 to 27,462 in 2020, and the 2025 Census estimate is 31,396. The 2020 census counted 11,195 households and 12,157 housing units, of which 7.9% were vacant.

The rental vacancy rate of 10.6% is higher than the owner vacancy rate. An owner with a rental house should expect a tenant search to take longer than a sale to a buyer that does not need a tenant.

sections.h2: What hurricane and flood risks affect a Daphne house?
sections.html:
Daphne's coastal setting brings tropical storm risk, and Hurricane Ivan, a Category 3 storm that made landfall in September 2004 near Gulf Shores, caused widespread flooding and damage in Daphne. Hurricane Danny in July 1997 pushed so much water out of Mobile Bay that it was almost possible to walk across it, and Katrina's effects the next year were milder.

Summers are warm and wet. Average highs reach 91 degrees in July and August, and annual rainfall is about 68 inches, with July the wettest month at roughly 8 inches.

Before a sale, owners usually gather:

  • Flood zone information and any elevation certificate for the house.
  • Homeowner and wind or flood insurance policies and recent claims.
  • Roof age, shutters and window condition.
  • Records of past storm repairs, with receipts.

Be ready for a buyer to ask about insurance cost, because on the coast it can shape what a buyer is willing to pay.

sections.h2: What does the Daphne economy look like?
sections.html:
Daphne is a suburb of Mobile, and primary employment is divided among education, health care and social assistance, with retail trade a close second. Agriculture, once a foundation of the economy, now accounts for less than 0.6% of economic output.

The Baldwin County Board of Education is the largest employer in the county, with more than 3,000 employees, and Thomas Hospital in Fairhope is about five miles south. The Daphne, Fairhope and Foley metro area was named among the top ten in the nation by Site Selection magazine for areas under 200,000 people. Large retail sits in Spanish Fort to the north.

sections.h2: Which schools and utilities serve Daphne?
sections.html:
Public schools belong to the Baldwin County Board of Education, with Daphne East Elementary, Daphne Elementary North Campus, W.J. Carroll Intermediate, Daphne Middle School and Daphne High School. Private options include Bayside Academy, Christ the King Catholic School and Bayshore Christian School.

  • Water, sewer and natural gas: Daphne Utilities.
  • Electricity: Riviera Utilities, based in Foley.
  • Fire: Daphne Fire Department. Police: Daphne Police Department.
  • Bus: Baldwin Rural Area Transportation Service.

The city has no rail or air service. Mobile Regional Airport and Pensacola International Airport handle most flights. Three exits from I-10 enter Daphne, at US 98, US 90 and AL 181.

sections.h2: What parks and local government affect a Daphne neighborhood?
sections.html:
Daphne is governed by a mayor and a seven-member council, all elected every four years, with a semi-autonomous Utilities Board and a Zoning Commission supporting the city. Zoning questions for a lot, an addition or a rental go through the Zoning Commission and city hall.

  • Daphne Sports Complex, a ten-field baseball and softball complex that opened in 2019.
  • Lott Park in Olde Towne, with tennis and pickleball courts added in 2020.
  • May Day Park, a waterfront park with a boat launch and a pier on Mobile Bay.
  • Village Point Park Preserve, the largest park, with trails and an estuary.
  • Bayfront Park, listed as closed until spring 2027.

The city also owns the Daphne Civic Center, which houses a senior activity center and the public library. Homes near the bay and the parks tend to be described by those landmarks, so name them in your listing or your offer request.

sections.h2: Who lives in Daphne, and what services are nearby?
sections.html:
The 2020 census found a median age of 40.1, with 22.5% of residents under 18 and 18.6% aged 65 or older. About 51.0% of households were married couples and 27.8% were one person living alone, and 99.6% of residents lived in urban areas.

Health care is close. Thomas Hospital in Fairhope is a 150-bed Level III hospital, Daphne has two urgent care facilities, and Mobile Bay Rehabilitation sits on the bay in the city. Across the water in Mobile there are several larger care facilities. Huntingdon College runs a graduate school in Daphne, and the United States Sports Academy is based here as well.

For a seller, that mix of families, retirees and commuters means two kinds of buyers: households who want school zones and parks, and older owners who want to be near medical care.

sections.h2: What happens at closing in Daphne?
sections.html:
A Baldwin County deed is filed with the probate judge, who figures the state recording tax at 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of that. The deed must show the actual purchase price, and any mortgage that already paid its own tax comes off the taxable amount.

The Alabama Department of Revenue lists property taxes as due October 1 and delinquent after December 31. Settle with your closing agent exactly who covers the current bill.

Sellers on the Eastern Shore usually weigh a listing against a direct sale. A listing can suit a turnkey house with clean insurance history. A direct as-is sale suits a house with storm damage, an out-of-area owner, or a probate sale, and we buy houses in Daphne without commissions or closing costs to you.

faqs.q: What county is Daphne, Alabama, in?
faqs.a: Daphne is in Baldwin County. It is the most populous city in the county.

faqs.q: Is Daphne the county seat of Baldwin County?
faqs.a: No. Daphne was the county seat from 1868 until a 1900 act moved it to Bay Minette.

faqs.q: Do hurricanes affect selling a house in Daphne?
faqs.a: They can. Hurricane Ivan in 2004 caused widespread flooding and damage in Daphne. Buyers ask about flood zones, insurance and past damage, so keep those records handy.

faqs.q: What is the Alabama deed recording tax?
faqs.a: It is 50 cents per $500 of value or fraction of $500, calculated by the probate judge when the deed is recorded, with mortgages that paid their own tax subtracted.

faqs.q: When are Alabama property taxes due?
faqs.a: The state revenue department says October 1, delinquent after December 31.
